what: The Pet Age Calculator turns your dog's or cat's age into human years. For dogs it uses the size-based chart published by the American Veterinary Medical Association, plus the newer epigenetic formula from a 2020 study. For cats it uses the widely used veterinary chart.
It also shows the old "× 7" rule and explains why the methods give different answers, along with your pet's life stage.
uses: See how old your pet is compared with a person.
Puppy, kitten, young adult, mature adult or senior.
Senior pets often need more frequent check-ups.
See why the × 7 rule is outdated.
tutorial: Type whole years and extra months (0–11).
For dogs, pick small, medium or large by adult weight.
See human years from the vet chart, the epigenetic formula (dogs), the × 7 rule and the life stage.
The "Why the numbers differ" table explains each method.
The age chart highlights the row nearest your pet's age.
features: Small, medium and large dogs from 1 to 16 years and beyond.
Puppies and kittens can be entered in months.

example.title: Worked example
example.text: A 5-year-old medium dog is about 36 in human years on the vet chart. The epigenetic formula gives 16 × ln(5) + 31 ≈ 57, and the × 7 rule gives 35. A 3-year-old cat is about 28 human years.

tips: Use your dog's adult weight to choose the size, even for a puppy.
Mixed breeds: choose the size closest to their adult weight.
Treat the numbers as a picture of life stage, not a health measure.
Ask your vet how often your pet needs check-ups at its stage.
problems: The formula is not meaningful for puppies under 1 year.
Months must be 0 to 11; put full years in the years box.
The result looks high for a giant breed
Giant breeds age even faster than the large-dog column; ask your vet.
